quest.title: The Funeral Parlor Has No Master, Yujing Terrace Calls the Troops
quest.description: The Lantern Rite has come around once more. What stories will be written in Liyue Harbor this year...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: The Funeral Parlor Has No Master, Yujing Terrace Calls the Troops

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Be extremely careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! It's us again, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Hello, you two. I'm so sorry, but if you're looking for the director, I'm afraid she still hasn't returned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? She still isn't back after two whole days?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that normal?

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: Hmm... Not exactly, but it's not unheard of. The director is unpredictable sometimes. She's been known to disappear for up to two weeks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, well in that case, a couple of days isn't a huge deal. Hu Tao will be Hu Tao...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: #Hey hey! I spy {NICKNAME} and a Paimon! Man, how long's it been? Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey, Gaming!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite, Gaming.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I gotta make a delivery to Chenyu Vale. It works out nicely, 'cause my dad's eager for me to get home for the holidays anyway. So, two birds with one stone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on! A delivery from the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor to Chenyu Vale? ...Is this for the Feiyun Commerce Guild, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: ...Wait, what? Have you been learning fortune-telling, or something? How could you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no. We just ran into Xingqiu a couple days ago, so he told us the news...

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Whew, you scared me there for a second! I thought we'd sprung a leak, and on the one job that we were specifically told has to be extremely hush-hush... But it sounds like you found out from another source, so we're all good.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Miss Undertaker, is everything ready to be loaded up? If so, I'll do a quick inventory count and then we'll be on our way.

dialogues.speaker: Ferrylady
dialogues.text: The goods are ready for inspection. This way, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Gaming... the last we heard, Baizhu was still trying to figure out a way to help Xingqiu's great-grandfather. So... did it not work, then?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Oh. The Baizhu part is news to me... but anyway, the master from the Feiyun Commerce Guild said they just wanna ship some items back home to get ahead of the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: I guess they're hoping for the best and planning for the worst. So don't worry, there's still hope.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ah, gotcha. Hey, {NICKNAME}, do you think we should go see Xingqiu?

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Uh, before you run off on a wild goose chase... Master Xingqiu's already back home in Chenyu Vale. He and his brother made the trip together — something about checking if any repairs are needed at the family home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... That doesn't sound promising...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's check in with Baizhu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! He's sure to know what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Gaming
dialogues.text: Alright, well I'd better get moving. Next time, we're going for dim sum!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Baizhu! What are the chances? We were just about to go looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: A most curious coincidence. He was searching for you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: #I was indeed. {NICKNAME}, there's a situation I need your help with.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has His Lordship taken a turn for the worse?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: No, his condition is stable for now. This is a different situation... it's about Qiqi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Qiqi? What's wrong with her? Has she passed out, too?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: She still hasn't come back from her herb-gathering trip. It was two days ago that she left, and she was supposed to return the same day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... um, maybe all the mountain-climbing slowed her down? Or maybe she got bored of work, and turned it into a vacation...?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Given Qiqi's unique condition, we always make sure to write the agreed return time in her notebook.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: There is also a rule in the notebook which says "Not finding herbs — OK. Getting home late — not OK." But she's now over a day late, and still, no sign of herbs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes... Has this ever happened before?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Never, hence our concern that something has happened to her. So, we posted a commission at the Adventurers' Guild yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: But I've dealt with many adventurers in the past, and they don't always fill me with confidence, so I'm not comfortable leaving the search for Qiqi to them alone.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Neither am I. Just this morning, some of the adventurers were back already, saying they found the place where Qiqi went missing, but got spooked because it was haunted. Needless to say, they did not catch a glimpse of Qiqi herself.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: In short, right now, you are the only person I feel I can trust completely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where did you send her to go herb-gathering?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Wuwang Hill, in the Qingce mountain range.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Qingce again, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Indeed... It's looking increasingly likely that something untoward has happened up there.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I saw two new patients yesterday. Their symptoms were identical to those present in Timaeus and His Lordship.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can discuss that later. Right now, we should go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, finding Qiqi is the number-one priority right now. We'll update you as soon as we can.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Thank you both. I'm counting on you.

talks.objective: Go to Wuwang Hill and search for Qiqi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That was fast!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: The border should be nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So, do you know the spell to open the border?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: No. Balancing the forces of life and death has always been the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's domain. I am not familiar with their craft.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: But since the border has been disrupted, fetor is leaking out. We simply need to find where the leak is — that will be your entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Evil Conquering!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was amazing... So you can see fetor?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: With my adeptus perception, I can sense the presence of the abnormal. Whether it's fetor or not, we shall see soon enough. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! It's another one of Lan Yan's rattan figures... Does that mean she's been here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Probably. And likely with Hu Tao.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just what are they up to...? Oh, Paimon's got it! They came here to go ghost-hunting!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The people from the Adventurers' Guild did say Wuwang Hill was haunted. Hu Tao knows all about ghosts, and Lan Yan's rattan figures have all those witness sigils on them, so she must know what she's doing too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then... what happened to Qiqi?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... One second, hmm... Okay, hear Paimon out. Qiqi's a zombie, so her joints are stiff. That means she can't run too fast, and so... she must have gotten kidnapped by a ghost!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A perfectly logical argument. But somehow, still not very credible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, alright then, well let's keep looking for clues. We'll see who's right soon enough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What was that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! Ghost incoming!

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Hold up. It's me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Yelan!? What are you doing here? We were told this place was haunted... Well, guess it kind of was. Just not by ghosts, apparently...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's right. I managed to scare off a few rookie adventurers, but it looks like you're not so easy to spook. Anyway, don't go any further — there's danger up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... we have to find Qiqi! She went missing around here, and she could be in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I'm aware of the situation. My contacts in the Adventurers' Guild filled me in.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I found an herb-gatherer's basket part way up the mountain, possibly belonging to Qiqi. But I don't think she's here anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What makes you so sure?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Because I scoured this whole place looking for clues. That's how I know that the immediate area is safe — but beyond this point, I can't be sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're here to look for Qiqi as well?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: No. I'm investigating the unknown disturbance here.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: About a month ago, the Ministry of Civil Affairs noticed an unusual spike in the number of elderly people seeking medical care in Qingce Village. Plus, they all seemed to be suffering from an unknown illness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Baizhu noticed that too! He's convinced that something's up in Qingce Village.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Actually, we discovered that the source of the problem isn't Qingce Village itself, but where we are now — Wuwang Hill.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: But the village isn't far from here, and the elderly residents are particularly vulnerable, which is why they've borne the brunt of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. The plot thickens.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll bet Hu Tao and Lan Yan knew something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Probably. If only we knew where the heck they've gone...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I... might have some idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really!? So where are they?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Somewhere difficult to reach. For now, you should come with me — we need to speak with Ningguang.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Don't act so surprised. I just shared top-secret information with you... Surely you didn't think I would let you walk away?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Wh—What are you gonna do!?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I'm kidding. Ningguang is well aware of the situation with Director Hu, and everything I've seen suggests that Lan Yan and Qiqi have ended up in the same place as her.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Come on. Ningguang will explain everything.

talks.objective: Examine the rattan figures near the monsters

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: In the past, I would've said "No way"...

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: I mean, I'd be happy to join you, but I'm not about to tell my crew they won't get to go home for the festival this year.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: That all goes without saying... unlike what I hope you're going to say next.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Haha! You sure have a way with words... alright, fine! It's a yes!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: The Gate of Fright, Guyun Stone Forest, yeah? I'll handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I knew I could count on the great Captain Beidou to answer the call of duty.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Save the compliments — just make sure you pay my crew properly. It's Lantern Rite, so they'll be expecting fives times their usual rate.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hah, the deal is sealed and then the trap is sprung... Well, you've got me now. So what about your share, hmm? How much will that rob me of?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Oh, please. Firstly, no one can rob the Tianquan — not even me. And secondly... Keep my share, it's my gift to you. Go buy yourself a new hairpin with it.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Saves me a trip to the market, right? Hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: #Oh, hey! {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahoy there, Captain Beidou!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Ah, little Paimon. That bright-eyed enthusiasm is exactly what Ningguang needs... She's conscripting you, by the way. Got some real back-breaking work lined up for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: Haha, sorry, I gotta dash. See ya 'round, folks!

dialogues.speaker: Beidou
dialogues.text: ...Oh yeah, and Happy Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Yelan clearly knows me well. She's brought you two here without me needing to say a word.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Beidou said you were... conscripting us?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Beidou never passes on an opportunity to wisecrack at my expense.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: #She's not exactly wrong though, is she? {NICKNAME} and Paimon have actually been there before. That makes them the perfect candidates.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Been where? Where's "there"?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I know you're looking for someone, and I don't wish to waste your time. So, I'll get right to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: From what I understand, Director Hu Tao, Miss Qiqi, and Ms. Lan Yan are currently stranded inside... the border.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Border... THE border? That border!?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Yes, that border. The border between life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa. When did you find out about the border? Wait, and how did you know we'd been there before?

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Heh. Come on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... literally your job to know that kind of stuff... Fair enough. Good job.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are you so sure they're at the border?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Time is limited, so I can't go into full detail, but let me give you a brief bit of background on the current situation.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: One month ago, the Ministry of Civil Affairs became aware of an unusual illness affecting the elderly of Qingce.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: A couple of weeks later, Director Hu came to report a potential disturbance in the border. The Ministry of Civil Affairs investigated, and sure enough, found an ominous presence on Wuwang Hill.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Then, three days ago, Hu Tao came to us again, this time to update us that she was now ready to go to the border and investigate the situation in full.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: We had agreed to meet again yesterday, but she failed to show up. That's when I sent Yelan to investigate further.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Director Hu's last-known location was Wuwang Hill. Same goes for Qiqi and Lan Yan. I'm about ninety percent sure all three of them are stuck in the border.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If even Hu Tao can't get out, there must be something seriously wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Now that you know the situation, are you willing to travel to the border and rescue Hu Tao and company? Your prior experience exploring that realm makes you our best hope.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! If our friends are in trouble, we'll help however we can!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there's one problem. Last time we went to the border, Hu Tao led the way. We don't know how to get there on our own.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm guessing Ningguang already thought of that?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: You can seek assistance from the Conqueror of Demons at Wangshu Inn. He will show you the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Xiao! Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Heh, Yelan was preparing to travel to the border herself before you two entered the picture. So naturally, he has been briefed on the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Understood. We will head out right away.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: This rescue mission is of the utmost importance. Director Hu must be brought back safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Consider it done.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Then I'll wait here for the good news.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: We got lucky. If I'd gone, I don't know what my chances would have been.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Mm, but don't go putting your feet up just yet, Yelan... I'm afraid I have another mission for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: ...Yeah, I figured that might be the case. What's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: The gate array. We've now found the locations of the gates of Life, Concealment, Fright, and Injury.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Keqing and Ganyu are handling the gates of Life and Concealment, and Captain Beidou has agreed to take the Crux Fleet to guard the Gate of Fright.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: That leaves the Gate of Injury. I've racked my brains, and other than the Conqueror of Demons, I can't think of anyone more suitable for this one than you.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: ...I see. It's in The Chasm.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: That's right. As for the remaining four gates, we are working to calculate their positions based on what we know of the array so far. It shouldn't take long now.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: When I last saw Director Hu, she said that if worse comes to worst, activating the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Array may be our only option.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: ...But if you have doubts, I would like to hear them.

dialogues.speaker: Yelan
dialogues.text: I don't know much about this magic array. But doesn't it involve obfuscating one of the people involved?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: *sigh* That is what troubles me, too... Let's continue this discussion another time.

talks.objective: Seek assistance from the Conqueror of Demons at Wangshu Inn

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xiao! You're already here.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...It's you two? Where's Yelan?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's been a change of plan.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea how dangerous this mission is?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We'll be fine. Danger's never stopped {NICKNAME} before, has it?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: The border between life and death is a treacherous place at the best of times, and the recent disturbances will only make it more so. You will face great peril at every step of the way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are people stranded there. We have to get them back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly. Plus, we made a promise to Ningguang.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: ...Please, go back and tell them to send Yelan instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? Are we not good enough?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: #I would feel more comfortable sending Yelan. She is privy to a secret art practiced by her clan, plus, she has extensive experience in battle. If anything was to happen to {NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ohh, so you're just worried for {M#his}{F#her} safety. Wait, but {F#s}he has extensive experience in battle too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, think of something!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We... promised Zhongli we would go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Show Xiao the Rex Coin from Zhongli)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Oh! Yeah, so um... This is a protective talisman that Zhongli gave us. It's even got the symbol of Rex Lapis on it — see?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He said we'd better get Hu Tao back safe and sound, or there'll be consequences!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Your attempts to mislead me are futile. That coin is clearly a counterfeit — it carries only the symbol of Rex Lapis, and none of his power.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Uh, drat! Zhongli swindled us, hehe... heh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's worrying you, Xiao?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I fear the bad karma I carry would only disturb the border further. So, while I can show you to the entrance... I cannot venture inside with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what this is about. You're worried that you won't be able to rescue us if something bad happens, huh? Paimon can understand, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not the one you should be worried about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Hu Tao understands the border better than anyone. Without her, no one has a clue how to handle this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Plus, we've been there before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! That makes us the second most experienced border-goers after Hu Tao!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dare to trust us.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Very well. Then, hold tight.

talks.objective: Find the source of the fetor
Enter the border between life and death

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: This is the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like it was fetor you saw back there after all.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: As I said earlier, this is as far as I can accompany you, or I risk doing more harm than good. You'll be on your own from here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry. We'll be okay.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Hmm... Lean your head in for a second.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Kavirudhaka! Huh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What did you do?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I placed a Witness Sigil on your forehead so you can share my powers of perception. Now you'll be able to see the fetor. There's no knowing what things are like in there, but hopefully this will help.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: When you find them, call my name. I will open a passage and pull you out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks Xiao, you've thought of everything! Back in a jiffy!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Be extremely careful.

talks.objective: Enter the border between life and death

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Guys, seriously — go rest and relax while you can! We have a big job coming up in two days' time.

talks.objective: Find the three people who are trapped
Find the three people who are trapped
Find the three people who are trapped

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I'm sleepy...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Don't fall asleep, Qiqi! You've already absorbed too much fetor. If you fall asleep, you'll never wake up again!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: But... so sleepy...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Focus on my voice, Qiqi. You are not feeling sleepy. You are the most awake person in the whole world. Even if everyone else falls asleep, you are going to stay wide awake.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Whole world, asleep... Qiqi, awake...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That was impressive. I didn't know hypnotism worked in reverse.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Even so, it doesn't really solve anything...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hang in there. I'm close to figuring out how to get to the exit.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Want to... close my eyes... and dream...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Fight it, Qiqi, fight it!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: A dream, huh? Alright, Qiqi, lemme help you with that. Now listen closely, this is how your dream is going to go:

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Picking herbs in the blazing sun, Qiqi wipes her brow.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Picking herbs... Qiqi...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: She finds a temple on a hill, and goes to seek the Dao.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Temple... on a hill...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: An old priest greets her at the door — surprise! Her name's Hu Tao!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: H—Hu Tao?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: She grabs young Qiqi with both hands... and buries her deep underground! By Rex Lapis, she'll never be found!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: No! Don't bury me! Help...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Not so sleepy now, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: No, wide awake with fright...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Drat... Hu Tao, we've got a problem. Somehow, they've broken through my illusion!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The monsters, you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Monsters...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Don't be afraid, Qiqi. We'll protect you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hu Tao! Madame Lan, Qiqi! Oh, thank goodness we finally found you!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: What the...? Oh, so it was you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: You frightened me for a second — I thought my illusion had been undone by a bunch of monsters... How did you find this place?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Let me guess, the Tianquan sent you? I knew she'd act if I missed our meeting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so Hu Tao really planned ahead! She knew someone would come after her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's dangerous here. Time to get out.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: It's not as simple as that. This place is changing constantly. Director Hu has found the exit plenty of times, but it would always close before we can get to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't worry, we've got you covered!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Call Xiao's Name)

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: You... found them?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh, the Conqueror of Demons is coming? Why, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: No need... I'll open the passage now...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: M—Monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Drat. They must have sensed the new way out.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hmph, let 'em come — it's their funeral. Courtesy of Director Hu.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: This will take me a minute or so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hurry, we've got to fend them off!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I'll help too.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: You have an update for me already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... no, we were just about to head off actually!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, you see, Xiao? Told you we'd be fine!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I'm glad you made it out.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Sir, but are you the legendary Conqueror of Demons?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: You may spare the formalities. Is everyone okay?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We're alright, but Qiqi absorbed a little too much fetor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Start from the beginning. What exactly happened?

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I was picking herbs. Then I saw a hole.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: I tried to block the hole...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: But instead, I fell in.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: There's clearly something special about Qiqi. If I'd absorbed that much fetor, I don't think I'd still be around to tell the tale...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Qiqi's condition is certainly... unique. But regardless, it was still a risky call.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well then, let's get her to Bubu Pharmacy, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: I'll take her. Your work is still not done, so you should return to Yujing Terrace.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, true. We shouldn't keep Ningguang waiting any longer. She's probably as stressed as a slime in a hot spring by this point, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...I highly doubt it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, well, we can discuss that later — let's just head back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ningguang, Ningguang! We got everyone back safely!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: #Impressive work, {NICKNAME}. You were even quicker than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought you'd be super anxious, having to wait for us here at Yujing Terrace. But you seem as calm as ever...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See? And you thought she'd be hopping around like a slime.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hehe, if I can't trust you, then I really don't know who I can turn to.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: My apologies, Lady Tianquan! I promise I'm not usually late for appointments, let alone by a whole day... Hope you can understand!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: No apology necessary, Director Hu. It was my mistake letting you go to the border by yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Don't say that! Even I didn't think the situation would get this bad.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How bad is "this bad"?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I'd like to know, too. How dangerous is the situation we face? And how does it compare to previous cases?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Way worse. Like waaaaaay, way worse!

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Huh? So this isn't the first time? I've never heard of this happening before...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well, don't forget, the border isn't part of the natural landscape. It's more like an old house that's gradually falling apart.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So it requires maintenance every once in a while — sometimes every few centuries, sometimes every other decade or so. And of course, that is the responsibility of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: In the past, though, the worst it got was a few small fetor leaks. That's an easy fix with our secret art — it burns it all away no problem. But this time is different... Inside the border, it's like the whole world has been turned upside down...

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea what the cause might be?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Not so far, no.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe it's the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I doubt it. I haven't found any traces of Abyssal activity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're thinking about Natlan, right? It did feel kind of similar... But not exactly the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Liyue's border anything like the Night Kingdom in Natlan?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Ah yes, I've heard a little about the crisis there. But as far as I understand, the Night Kingdom is a true realm of the dead, while the border is more of a boundary world between life and death.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yep. It's a demarcation line: life on one side, death on the other. So if the border fails, souls will pour out, and the whole thing becomes a chaotic mix of life and death. Just like what happened all those millennia ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder so many people have been aging faster than normal...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: It's a symptom of death encroaching on the world of the living.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Then, what should we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Burning away the fetor won't do any good, because the issue is the border itself. Lady Tianquan, any progress on the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method I mentioned last time?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Yes. We've deduced the locations of four of the gates, and we should be able to pinpoint the rest of the array before long.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Whoa, already? The Tianquan doesn't mess around!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Several strokes of luck were involved. Our nation is blessed with good fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second! That gates method you mentioned... are you talking about the one from the Sanctification of Tao Dou!?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's the one. You've seen the state of the border. I can't think of any other way to fix it besides a complete do-over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do-over? You mean, make a whole new border?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: No, no, not the whole border — just the part that's been giving us grief. Which is just as well — reconstructing the whole thing would be much more difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is this Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The eight gates refer to eight key nodes in Liyue's Ley Lines: Life, Death, Repose, Concealment, Initiation, Terrain, Fright, and Injury. They can be used to direct the Ley Lines' energy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the seven?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's the requirement for activating the array. The array master will select one gate from the eight to subdue evil, cutting off its exit path by using the Ley Lines' power to obfuscate themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What do you mean, "obfuscate"?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: As in, disappear from the Ley Lines completely, never to be seen again — taking the banished evil along with them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... so someone has to die for this to work? But... you can't seriously be considering this?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Now, now, don't worry! That's the traditional interpretation, but people just assumed that because the Lone Butterfly sacrificed herself.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: But let's not forget, they were purifying a whole god! As bad as things are now, it's still a far cry from what they had to deal with. Besides, the border isn't completely ruined, so we're only fixing one part of it.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: If you ask me, as long as the array master can withstand a huge blast of fetor, they'll be just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Oh? Do you have any proof to back up this statement, Director Hu?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: My proof is that I know the most about life and death out of everybody here! Unless anyone wants to dispute that?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: ...No one? Okay good. Looks like we're all in agreement. In that case, we can plan our next steps as soon as the Tianquan has found the remaining four gates.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Director Hu...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hmm? Something to add, Lady Tianquan?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: No... There is something else that I'd like to ask about, but it might not be my place to do so. If you do not wish to answer, then please pretend I never said anything.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Sure, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Do you believe that today's border crisis could have anything to do with the Wuwang Hill Disaster from over a decade ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? There was a disaster at Wuwang Hill? What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Some sort of natural disaster, wasn't it? There used to be a village there, but then there was a flood or something. It took a lot of lives, and all the survivors moved away.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Hmm... But that doesn't explain how Wuwang Hill became the dark and gloomy place it is today. Maybe there was... more to it?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: No, Lady Tianquan. I don't think these two events are related.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Excellent, well that puts my mind at ease. Everyone, let's meet here again in two days. We should know the locations of all the gates by then.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Alright. Well, I've still got a lot of preparations to make, so I'll be heading back to the funeral parlor now.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Sounds good. If we're all done here, I'd better get going too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Lan Yan, Paimon meant to ask. How did you know where to find Hu Tao? Did you already know something was wrong with the border?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Oh, haha, that? Yeah, I definitely owe you an explanation. Why don't you meet me at the Adventurers' Guild later? I just need to write a letter to my family first. I want to let them know I'm fine, and I also have some questions I want to ask them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, then we'll see you at the Adventurers' Guild!

talks.objective: Meet Lan Yan at the Adventurers' Guild

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! Over here! Perfect timing — I literally just posted my letter.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Anyway, back to your question... Let me guess, you're probably thinking I predicted the border crisis with some kind of mysterious magic?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, yeah. Aren't the Lans of Chenyu Vale all experts at Qimen Divination, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: *sigh* No, that's simply not true. Yes, the Qimen arts have been practiced in my clan for many generations, and yes, Wind Reader is listed as one of our ancestors in the genealogy...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: But my family are only distant relatives — we branched off from the main family line long ago. By my grandpa's generation, the only Qimen he knew was a few parlor tricks.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Put it like this — my grandpa makes a living telling fortunes in Yilong Wharf, but I'm making more than him just selling my handmade arts and crafts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So why exactly did you come to look for Hu Tao?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Because Grandpa's readings have gone sideways recently. The romance and career fortunes are doing okay, but when it comes to longevity, everyone's reading is suddenly saying they only have a few years left to live. It gave grandpa quite a fright.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Fearing backlash from his clients, he closed shop and shut himself away at home, trying to divine an answer to the strange readings. But after days and nights of divination, the only clue he got was: "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor."

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Right around that time, I happened to receive an invitation from the Ministry of Civil Affairs to organize a street fair. So, I figured I might as well drop by the funeral parlor to see what Director Hu might know about all this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Wait, so... Your grandpa's divinations were correct all along, weren't they? The longevity readings were affected by the border crisis, and "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor" was the answer, because they can fix it!

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: It's certainly looking that way. Apparently, every soul in Liyue is now living under the creeping shadow of death, but so far, we are the only ones in the know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have another question. What's the deal with this rattan figure?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Wait, that's the one I left at Miss Ying'er's shop... It's actually a product of genuine Qimen art. It's engraved with an exorcism sigil to absorb inauspicious energy in their owner's place, so they won't come to harm.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I had no idea you'd been holding onto it all this time... Haha, I guess it was meant to be. You're more than welcome to keep it if you like.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: When I first arrived in Liyue Harbor, I passed by a large house, and felt a chill go down my spine. So I made a rattan figure, and gave it to the young master there.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Later on, I also sensed something similar around Timaeus, so I made another one, and left it at Scent of Spring.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Then, I followed Director Hu to Wuwang Hill, only to find she'd disappeared without a trace. While I was searching the area, I found Miss Qiqi. She was stuck in some kind of crevice, and she seemed to be blocking something from coming through.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: When I tried to pull her out, we both got pulled in to a cold, dark place... which, I soon discovered, was the border.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: We wandered around aimlessly for a while until we ran into Director Hu. She'd lit some incense and was burning fetor left and right with a flaming staff.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: But there was just too much... There was no way she could hope to get rid of it all. Worse still, the fetor blocked off the way we'd come in, trapping us inside. Thank goodness you came to our rescue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, what an ordeal... Still, your family sounds more impressive than you let on — didn't you use some kind of illusion magic in the border?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. Actually, that and the rattan figures are things I learned from one of my cousins in the main branch of my family. She's been practicing the Qimen arts since she was little. She's also the one I posed some questions to in my letter back home.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Questions about the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Wow. Good guess... Yes, I want to know for sure whether sacrificing one of the participants is a necessary part of the method or not. I figured she might know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But Hu Tao already told us it won't come to that... She said we just need to make sure the person can withstand a strong blast of fetor.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Mm... I certainly hope that's true, but I can't help but feel uneasy about it. I haven't known Director Hu for long, but... I get the sense that she prefers to keep the truth bottled up sometimes.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Sure, she talks a lot, and isn't afraid to broach dark and uncomfortable topics. But she really hasn't said much in the way of her own, private thoughts. It's like she's already got a plan, and is keeping it to herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean... You think she lied to us...?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I wouldn't call it "lying," per se, but... remember when the Tianquan asked about the incident at Wuwang Hill from a decade ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Hu Tao said that it doesn't have anything to do with what's happening now. Are you saying they actually are related?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know anything about what happened back then, Lan Yan?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I just heard that there was a flood. But given everything that's going on, I think it likely had to do with the border as well. That would at least explain the strange weather going on at Wuwang Hill.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I remember my cousin saying that around that time, the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor set up an altar on top of the hill. I just assumed it was for a funeral, but now, I can't help but wonder if it was some sort of ritual to try and fix the border.

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Anyway, the ceremony was hosted jointly by two former directors of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. Namely, Hu Tao's father and grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, really? Hu Tao's never mentioned her dad to us before... How strange. So you think there's more to this story, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: Yeah... But since she brushed it aside when the Tianquan asked her about it, I don't see how I can broach the topic. I've only known her for a few days...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess we should go talk to Hu Tao ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You think we should ask her about it? But she's never opened up to us about family stuff before... What if she shuts us out?

choices.text: Then that's her choice. All we can do is try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Alright, let's go find her, and take it from there...

choices.text: Then you can keep poking her till she tells us the truth.

talks.objective: Visit Hu Tao at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hu Tao!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! What's up? We haven't spoken in five minutes and you're missing me already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! So we thought we'd come hang out with you. What were you looking at just now?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Something so amazing, you wouldn't believe it. But I'm not showing you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why? ...Is it a secret photo of me?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Seriously though, you probably shouldn't joke about that. You don't wanna jinx it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jinx it how?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well, the people in this picture keep appearing in my dreams lately, and none of them are around anymore... So keeping you out of the picture is probably for the best.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Haha, alright, I'll quit joking around. Here, take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, are they...?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yeah, my dad and my grandpa. Without this picture, I'd probably have forgotten what my dad looked like by now. When he passed, I was still too young to understand what was going on.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Everything I know about my dad, I learned from my grandpa.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... what happened to him?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: There was a border incident on Wuwang Hill about a dozen years ago. My dad tried using the Art of Homa to burn away the fetor, but he slipped up and suffered a lethal exposure to it. He died on the spot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's awful... So, is that what made Wuwang Hill the way it is today?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yep. His mistake didn't just cost him his own life — it took most of the village out, and left lasting changes on Wuwang Hill itself.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Thankfully, my grandpa managed to deal with the fallout — but that's not to say he escaped unscathed... He didn't even make it to sixty before he passed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So your grandpa was affected by the incident with your dad?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well, he never admitted it, of course. But given how fit and healthy he was before that, I would've expected him to have a few more years in him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like... You blame your dad for all of this...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: How could I not? It would be one thing if he was just a spoiled brat who never amounted to anything. But he was a genius. He was, and still is, the best spellcaster in our family for generations.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Grandpa always called me gifted for mastering the Wangsheng arts by the age of eight, but by the time my dad was eight, he was already hosting rituals and incinerating fetor all by himself.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Fixing the border crisis should have been a piece of cake for him, and he messed up. Who else is there to blame, if not him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... Maybe the question is, why did he mess up?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Because he was an unworthy director. Every past director has burned away all of their belongings when they pass on, leaving at most one or two items behind.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: My grandpa, for example, left only his hat behind. But my dad? He left a whole pile of stuff, including this meaningless picture...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But doesn't that just show how much he cared...?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: No — all it shows is that he was unable to let go. And the fact that he couldn't let go is precisely why he failed during that ritual.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: He was too attached to his aging father, his young daughter, and the world where we were all together.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's why he hesitated in that final moment. Because he was afraid to die, he lost focus, and death won, taking his life and many others.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: In this line of work, we know better than anyone how hard letting go can be. We see it all the time. But as funeral directors, it's the one thing we cannot allow ourselves to fall victim to.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Like Grandpa always said, we should live in life, and die in death... That's the whole basis of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's existence.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, with my dad, these teachings went in one ear and out the other. He really let everyone down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't need to be so hard on him... Sure, he made a mistake, but he can't have meant for things to turn out this way.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You're missing the point, my little Paimon. It's precisely because he's my dad that I choose not to hold back.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: There isn't a father in the world who would disapprove of their daughter being outspoken. Because a father's biggest fear is that once he's not around anymore, his daughter will never get to be that carefree, sassy little kid ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So, I'm gonna keep talking trash about him all I want. And on the off chance he ever overhears me, I know he'll take some comfort from knowing that I never stopped just being myself and living my life my way.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Anyway, so that's a brief history of Wuwang Hill for you. Anything else on the agenda?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for being so open with us.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hehe, did you think I'd hide it from you? Nah, we're better buds than that.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Plus, you did just rescue me from the border, so I owe you bigtime. Answering your questions seems like the least I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Alright, in that case, Paimon has one last question! Earlier, you said that no one will have to die when the array is activated... Is that the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yes. In my highly professional opinion, yes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, phew. That's all Paimon wanted to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Try not to dwell too much on all this stuff, okay? There are still two days to go, so check out the street fair and enjoy yourself. You said it yourself, remember? Gotta keep a reasonable work-life balance.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I'll see you at Yujing Terrace in two days. This time, we're gonna turn death to ashes!

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's bothering you, Ningguang?

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: The Wuwang Hill Disaster has always haunted me... Still, if Director Hu says the incidents are unrelated, I probably shouldn't pry any further...

dialogues.speaker: Lan Yan
dialogues.text: I hope my family will write back to me soon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, it's been two whole days. Surely Hu Tao must have finished her work by now? Let's go to the funeral parlor and check.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon, or is this place creepier than ever? ...Paimon really hopes Qiqi's okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: The fetor has sent them into a frenzy... Stand back. I'll deal with them.
